Consumer & Culture Trends

Distorted Reality

The gap between curated, filtered, or manipulated media content and actual reality, especially as shaped by social media and retouched marketing imagery.

Explanation

Distorted reality describes how heavily edited photos, selectively curated feeds, and idealized marketing visuals can create a false or exaggerated impression of a product, lifestyle, or person. The concept is not tied to one coiner; it has been discussed for years in media literacy and marketing-ethics writing as digital editing tools and social platforms made manipulation cheap and widespread. Consumers increasingly notice and react against unrealistic imagery, and brands that lean on authenticity and unretouched content often build more durable trust than those relying on idealized visuals.

Related terms

Dark Social, Memevertising
